## Paper and figure

Reck, M., Rodríguez-Abreu, D., Robinson, A. G., et al. (2021). Five-Year Outcomes With Pembrolizumab Versus Chemotherapy for Metastatic Non–Small-Cell Lung Cancer With PD-L1 Tumor Proportion Score ≥ 50%. *Journal of Clinical Oncology*, **39**(21), 2339–2349. <https://doi.org/10.1200/JCO.21.00174>.

I reconstruct **Figure 2**, available in the [open-access paper](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8280089/#F2). It shows Kaplan–Meier curves for overall survival (OS; panel A) and progression-free survival (PFS; panel B). This figure interests me because the same treatment comparison can look different depending on the endpoint.

The figure meets four assignment criteria: **facets** determined by endpoint; **multiple layers** consisting of step curves and censoring ticks; **treatment mapped to color**; and **a computed quantity**, the Kaplan–Meier survival estimate. Both axes use ordinary linear scales.

## Part 1: Infer the data

### Variables and structure

The underlying data need one patient identifier, a treatment group, and an observed time and event indicator for each endpoint. The published trial has 305 patients: 154 assigned to pembrolizumab and 151 to chemotherapy. Both endpoints refer to the same patients, not separate samples.

| Variable | Type | Meaning and plausible values |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | Identifier | Unique integers from 1 to 305 |
| `treatment` | Categorical | Pembrolizumab or Chemotherapy |
| `endpoint` | Categorical | Overall survival or Progression-free survival |
| `time` | Continuous | Months from randomization to an event or censoring; positive and approximately below 69 |
| `status` | Binary categorical | 1 for an observed endpoint event; 0 for right censoring |

For OS, the event is death. For PFS, it is progression or death, whichever occurs first. A censored observation records how long the patient was observed without that endpoint event; it does not imply that the event happened at that time. For plotting, I reshape the patient data into 610 patient–endpoint records.

### Relationships and a reproducible generative model

Both curves should start at 100%, decline in steps, and generally remain higher for pembrolizumab. PFS should decline earlier than OS. The paper reports median OS of 26.3 and 13.4 months and median PFS of 7.7 and 5.5 months for pembrolizumab and chemotherapy, respectively. I use these as population targets, without forcing the simulated sample medians to equal them.

I generate independent patients using the following model, with treatment-specific parameters listed in pembrolizumab/chemotherapy order:

1. Draw death time $D$ from a Weibull distribution with shape $k_D=0.70/0.78$ and scale $b_D=m_D/(\log 2)^{1/k_D}$, where $m_D=26.3/13.4$ months.
2. Independently draw progression time $G$ from a Weibull distribution with shape $k_G=0.48/0.90$. Choose its scale as $b_G=m_P/[\log 2-(m_P/b_D)^{k_D}]^{1/k_G}$, where $m_P=7.7/5.5$ months. Thus $P(\min(D,G)>m_P)=0.5$.
3. Draw administrative follow-up $C_A\sim U(55,69)$ months. Independently, with probability 0.10, generate earlier loss to follow-up $C_L\sim U(6,48)$; otherwise set $C_L=\infty$. Let $C=\min(C_A,C_L)$.
4. Record OS time $\min(D,C)$ and status $I(D\leq C)$, and PFS time $\min(D,G,C)$ and status $I(\min(D,G)\leq C)$.

### Simplifications

The Weibull shapes and censoring mechanism are my assumptions, not estimates from individual trial data. I ignore covariates, treatment crossover, assessment schedules, and the original endpoint-specific censoring rules. Progression and death are independent conditional on treatment, but the endpoints remain related through the shared death and censoring times, ensuring PFS never exceeds OS. I omit the original risk tables, reference guides, and numerical annotations while preserving both panels, curves, and censoring marks. These simulated data illustrate the graphic and cannot support clinical conclusions.

## Part 2: Rebuild the figure

### Seeded simulation

Only `ggplot2`, `survival`, and `colorspace` are needed in addition to Quarto's R dependencies. All data are generated below; no downloaded data or saved R workspace is required.

```{r}
#| label: simulate
seed <- 5014L
set.seed(seed)
library(ggplot2)
library(survival)

groups <- c("Pembrolizumab", "Chemotherapy")
sizes <- c(154L, 151L)
patients <- data.frame(id = seq_len(sum(sizes)),
                       treatment = factor(rep(groups, sizes), levels = groups))
g <- as.integer(patients$treatment)
n <- nrow(patients)
death_shape <- c(0.70, 0.78)[g]
death_scale <- c(26.3, 13.4)[g] / log(2)^(1 / death_shape)
pfs_median <- c(7.7, 5.5)[g]
progression_shape <- c(0.48, 0.90)[g]
progression_scale <- pfs_median /
  (log(2) - (pfs_median / death_scale)^death_shape)^(1 / progression_shape)
death <- rweibull(n, death_shape, death_scale)
progression <- rweibull(n, progression_shape, progression_scale)
administrative <- runif(n, 55, 69)
dropout <- ifelse(runif(n) < 0.10, runif(n, 6, 48), Inf)
censor <- pmin(administrative, dropout)
endpoints <- c("A. Overall survival", "B. Progression-free survival")
dat <- rbind(
  transform(patients, endpoint = endpoints[1], time = pmin(death, censor),
            status = as.integer(death <= censor)),
  transform(patients, endpoint = endpoints[2],
            time = pmin(death, progression, censor),
            status = as.integer(pmin(death, progression) <= censor))
)
dat$endpoint <- factor(dat$endpoint, levels = endpoints)
```

### Compute the survival estimates

At each event time, the Kaplan–Meier estimator multiplies the previous survival probability by the proportion of patients at risk who survive that time. Censoring reduces later risk sets without causing a downward step. The tick marks are placed at the estimated survival probability at each censoring time.

```{r}
#| label: estimate
km <- do.call(rbind, lapply(endpoints, function(e) {
  fit <- survfit(Surv(time, status) ~ treatment,
                 data = dat[dat$endpoint == e, ])
  s <- summary(fit, censored = TRUE)
  data.frame(endpoint = e, treatment = sub("^treatment=", "", s$strata),
             time = s$time, survival = s$surv, n_censor = s$n.censor)
}))
starts <- expand.grid(endpoint = endpoints, treatment = groups)
starts$time <- 0
starts$survival <- 1
starts$n_censor <- 0
km <- rbind(starts, km)
km$endpoint <- factor(km$endpoint, levels = endpoints)
km$treatment <- factor(km$treatment, levels = groups)
km <- km[order(km$endpoint, km$treatment, km$time), ]
```

### Reconstructed figure

The plotting block has approximately twenty lines. Blue and orange replace the original blue and red. I also map treatment to linetype so the groups remain identifiable without color.

```{r}
#| label: fig-reconstruction
#| fig-width: 7.5
#| fig-height: 8
palette <- c(Pembrolizumab = "#0072B2", Chemotherapy = "#D55E00")
line_types <- c(Pembrolizumab = "solid", Chemotherapy = "longdash")
p <- ggplot(km, aes(x = time, y = 100 * survival,
                    color = treatment, linetype = treatment)) +
  geom_step(direction = "hv", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = subset(km, n_censor > 0),
             shape = 124, size = 2.5, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(vars(endpoint), ncol = 1) +
  scale_color_manual(values = palette) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = line_types) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 72, 12),
                     expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.01))) +
  scale_y_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 100, 25), limits = c(0, 100)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 72)) +
  labs(x = "Time since randomization (months)",
       y = "Survival probability (%)", color = NULL, linetype = NULL) +
  theme_classic(base_size = 12) +
  theme(legend.position = "top", strip.background = element_blank(),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
        panel.spacing = grid::unit(1.1, "lines"))
p
```

::: {.figure-caption}
**Figure.** Simulated reconstruction of the selected published figure using `r nrow(patients)` patients (`r sizes[1]` assigned to pembrolizumab and `r sizes[2]` to chemotherapy), shown across `r length(endpoints)` endpoint panels. The same patients contribute to both panels. Step curves are Kaplan–Meier estimates, and vertical ticks mark censoring. Simulation seed: `r seed`. These are simulated outcomes, not the trial's patient data.
:::

### Colorblindness check

The following check simulates full-severity protanopia, deuteranopia, and tritanopia for the chosen palette. The resulting swatches remain distinguishable; solid and dashed lines provide an additional cue, including in grayscale.

```{r}
#| label: fig-palette-check
#| fig-width: 7.5
#| fig-height: 2.3
vision <- list("Original" = identity, "Protanopia" = colorspace::protan,
               "Deuteranopia" = colorspace::deutan, "Tritanopia" = colorspace::tritan)
op <- par(mar = c(1, 9, 1, 1))
plot.new()
plot.window(xlim = c(0, 2), ylim = c(0, 4))
for (i in seq_along(vision)) {
  rect(0:1, 4 - i, 1:2, 4.8 - i, col = vision[[i]](unname(palette)), border = NA)
  text(0, 4.4 - i, names(vision)[i], pos = 2, xpd = NA)
}
par(op)
```

## One improvement to the original

The original figure could use distinct line patterns for the treatment groups so readers can distinguish them without relying on color.
